title: Colimit coherence of a transported graded scalar-extension map
statement: Let I be a preorder, F : I → CRing [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], i₀ ∈ I, and P,Q cochain complexes of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let i,j ≥ i₀ with i ≤ j, and vⁿ arbitrary graded maps from Pᵢⁿ to Qᵢⁿ. Let c be the natural scalar-extension comparison from direct extension i₀ → j to extension through i, using functoriality of F, and let eᵢ,eⱼ be the canonical complex comparisons from direct extension i₀ → colimit F to extension through i,j. For wⁿ = c_Pⁿ followed by extension of vⁿ from i to j followed by the inverse of c_Qⁿ, conjugating extension of wⁿ to the colimit by eⱼ equals conjugating extension of vⁿ by eᵢ, in every degree. There are no finite-presentation, directedness or chain-square hypotheses.

proof.text: For ring maps f : R → S, g : S → T, h : T → A, evaluate ModuleCat.extendScalars_assoc at M and N. It equates the two isomorphisms from direct extension R → A to iterated extension R → S → T → A. Equality of their inverses and naturality_2 of extendScalarsComp g h show that extending the conjugate of v by extendScalarsComp f g and then conjugating to direct extension equals conjugating its direct S → A extension.

Allow additional ring maps k : R → T, r : R → A, s : S → A with k = g.comp f, r = s.comp f, s = h.comp g. Substitute these equalities. The remaining equation r = h.comp k is reflexive by associativity, so its eqToIso is the identity. The complex components reduce to the module identity in the preceding step.

Specialize to the transition ring maps i₀ → i → j and the colimit cocone. F.map_comp gives the first relation and colimit.w gives the others. Apply the comparison identity independently to each v n. No finite-presentation or commutativity hypotheses are involved.

theorem graded_scalarExtension_colimit_coherence
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ)
    (i j : Set.Ici i₀) (hij : i.val ≤ j.val)
    (hc : (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom =
      (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom.comp (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom)
    (v : ∀ n : ℤ,
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (P.X n) ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).obj (Q.X n)) :
    let c := eqToIso (congrArg ModuleCat.extendScalars hc) ≪≫
      ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom
        (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom
    let e (t : Set.Ici i₀) (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ) :=
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun r ↦
        ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)
        (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE t.property)).symm)) ≪≫
      (NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
        (ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp (F.map (homOfLE t.property)).hom
          (colimit.ι F t.val).hom) (.up ℤ)).app C
    ∀ n : ℤ, (e j P).hom.f n ≫
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F j.val).hom).map
        (c.hom.app (P.X n) ≫
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom).map (v n) ≫
            c.inv.app (Q.X n)) ≫ (e j Q).inv.f n =
      (e i P).hom.f n ≫
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i.val).hom).map (v n) ≫
          (e i Q).inv.f n
